summary: Arizona 'Ma' Barker raised four criminal sons in Missouri and Oklahoma, sheltered fugitives, and helped steer the Barker-Karpis Gang's 1930s kidnappings from St. Paul until the FBI killed her in Florida in 1935.

evidence.note: Arizona Clark born 1873 in Greene County, Missouri; main source named
family moves to Tulsa in 1910; sons soon on the police blotter
host contrasts FBI account with historians and gangster myth-making
long segment on Herman Barker's own gang and robberies
Herman kills an officer, is wounded in a chase and shoots himself
St. Paul police corruption under the O'Connor layover deal
Alvin Karpis joins and the Barker-Karpis gang forms around Ma
Ma's abusive partner Arthur Dunlop, later killed by the gang
crude fingerprint and face surgery on gang members described
FBI shootout at Lake Weir, Florida, January 1935 kills Ma and Fred

notes: Vocabulary gap: no theme for organized crime, bank robbery or kidnapping; policing-incarceration (FBI pursuit, jailbreaks, bribed police, St. Paul corruption) plus the criminal-org subject carry it, hence themes low. folklore-legend reflects the debate over whether she was a mastermind or an FBI myth. Transcript drops several years; lifespans filled from general knowledge.
